narrative.title: Seating a Jury Pool from Nine Fixed Candidates
narrative.scenario: A court coordinator seats a jury of exactly k members whose seniority scores add up to a required total n, drawing from a fixed candidate bench numbered 1 through 9. Each candidate serves at most once, and the roster must be complete — exactly k names, no fewer. The coordinator walks the bench once per slot: seat the current candidate and shrink the target, or pass on them for good.
narrative.inputFormat: Two integers k (roster size) and n (required sum).
narrative.outputFormat: Every k-member combination from 1..9 summing to n, sorted lexicographically by the verifier.

complexity.optimalTime: O(2^9) — the bench is fixed at nine candidates
complexity.optimalSpace: O(k) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: 1 + 2 + 4 is the only three-member roster reaching 7.
Three rosters: the smallest three plus two, or mid-weight trades around them.

hintLevels: Level 1: Two budgets shrink simultaneously — the remaining sum and the number of picks left; success requires both to land exactly.
Level 2: A pick advances the index (no reuse); a pass advances it too. Record only when remaining hits 0 with picks == k.
Level 3: Prune hard: stop when remaining < 0, when picks exceed k, or when the bench cannot supply enough remaining numbers.
